examples.text: „Scholli“ ist eine Verballhornung von „Joly“.
Das Wort „Rutsch“ im Neujahrsgruß „Guten Rutsch!“ ist eine Verballhornung des hebräischen „Rosch (ha-Schanah)“ und bedeutet „Anfang“.
Die Redewendung „Unter aller Kanone“ ist eine Verballhornung des lateinischen „sub omni canone“, das wörtlich „unterhalb jeder Messskala“ bedeutet.
„Nicht nur, weil er das Gegenteil von jedem Siegfried war, eher klein, dunkel und witzig, sondern weil das Wort »Krümel« so etwas wie die Verballhornung seines Familiennamens darstellte.“
„Er will raus aus der Kitschecke, aus der Sphäre der Verniedlichung und der Verballhornung.“

glosses: The act of corrupting or of impairing integrity, virtue, or moral principle; the state of being corrupted or debased; loss of purity or integrity.

examples.text: It was necessary, by exposing the gross corruptions of monasteries, […] to exite popular indignation against them.

glosses: The act of corrupting or making putrid, or state of being corrupt or putrid; decomposition or disorganization, in the process of putrefaction; putrefaction; deterioration.

examples.text: The inducing and accelerating of putrefaction is a subject of very universal inquiry; for corruption is a reciprocal to generation.

glosses: The product of corruption; putrid matter.

examples.text: Think of wandering amid sepulchral ruins, of stumbling over the bones of the dead, of encountering what I cannot describe,—the horror of being among those who are neither the living or the dead;—those dark and shadowless things that sport themselves with the reliques of the dead, and feast and love amid corruption,—ghastly, mocking, and terrific.

examples.text: The idea of having a time lag is to allow for situations when a corruption of some type affects the source server. examples.text: The affix ty, like té, Fr., ta, It., dad, Sp., is a corruption of the Latin affix tas, tat, and Greek tes; as bounty, bonté, Fr., bonta, It., bondad, Sp., bonitas from bonus, good; vanity, vanité, Fr., vanita, It., vanidad, Sp, vanitas from vanus, vain.
